tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Page ground behind everything. Also the ground of the top bar and the queue footer.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Panels, tables, the editor, the graph canvas, popovers and dialogs. The one place content sits.

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Inputs, code and command blocks, plot areas, neutral state tags (queued, cancelled), the selected level in the level switch's track.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairlines: panel edges, table row separators, plot grid. Decorative separation only; never the only cue for a control.

tokens.name: line-strong
tokens.usage: Borders of controls that must be found (inputs, secondary buttons, checkboxes, drop slots). 3:1 or more on surface, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Primary text and values on surface, surface-raised, surface-sunken and every *-soft fill.

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary text: help text, units, metadata, axis labels, placeholder text. 4.5:1 or more on every ground in both themes; use it, never a lighter grey.

tokens.name: ink-disabled
tokens.usage: Disabled controls only (WCAG exempts them). Never for text a person needs to read.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Cobalt. Interactive and selected only: primary buttons, links, the selected tab and nav item, the focus ring, the selected graph node. Never a state, never a series, never decoration.

tokens.name: accent-strong
tokens.usage: Hover and pressed state of accent fills and links.

tokens.name: accent-soft
tokens.usage: Ground of a selected row, a selected palette item, or a drop slot under a dragged block. Text on it is ink or accent.

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text and icons on an accent or accent-strong fill (the primary button's label).

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: Keyboard focus ring: 2px solid, offset 2px from the control. An alias of accent, so it moves with it.

tokens.name: good
tokens.usage: State word and glyph for done, passed and 'better'. As text on any ground or good-soft. Never as the only cue: always with a glyph and a word.

tokens.name: good-soft
tokens.usage: Ground of a good state tag or a passed check result.

tokens.name: warn
tokens.usage: State word and glyph for stopped, cancelling, 'within noise' cautions and the library's notes shown as warnings. As text on any ground or warn-soft.

tokens.name: warn-soft
tokens.usage: Ground of a warn tag or a note shown as a warning.

tokens.name: bad
tokens.usage: State word and glyph for failed and 'worse', and for problem+json errors. As text on any ground or bad-soft. Destructive buttons use it as border and text, not as a fill.

tokens.name: bad-soft
tokens.usage: Ground of a failed tag, a failed check, or an error panel.

tokens.name: diff-del
tokens.usage: Removed lines in a diff (conflict dialog, swap preview), with a leading − sign. An alias of bad.

tokens.name: diff-del-soft
tokens.usage: Ground of a removed line in a diff.

tokens.name: diff-add
tokens.usage: Added lines in a diff, with a leading + sign. An alias of good.

tokens.name: diff-add-soft
tokens.usage: Ground of an added line in a diff.

tokens.name: series-1
tokens.usage: First data series (Okabe-Ito blue). Series colors identify a run or variant on a plot; they never judge it.

tokens.name: series-2
tokens.usage: Second data series (Okabe-Ito vermillion, darkened for light).

tokens.name: series-3
tokens.usage: Third data series (Okabe-Ito bluish green).

tokens.name: series-4
tokens.usage: Fourth data series (Okabe-Ito reddish purple).

tokens.name: series-5
tokens.usage: Fifth data series (Okabe-Ito orange, darkened for light).

tokens.name: series-6
tokens.usage: Sixth data series (Okabe-Ito sky blue). More than six series: use small multiples, not more hues.

tokens.name: baseline
tokens.usage: The baseline's line on a plot, drawn dashed. Neutral on purpose: the baseline is the reference, not a contender.

tokens.name: band
tokens.usage: The baseline band (shipped seeds' range) and CI whiskers' fill behind plot lines.

tokens.name: grid
tokens.usage: Plot grid lines and the forest plot's tick lines. Quieter than line on purpose.

tokens.name: heat-1
tokens.usage: Lowest step of the sequential scale (block stats on graph nodes, attention maps). Plum, chosen apart from accent and the state hues.

tokens.name: heat-2
tokens.usage: Second step of the sequential scale.

tokens.name: heat-3
tokens.usage: Middle step of the sequential scale.

tokens.name: heat-4
tokens.usage: Fourth step of the sequential scale.

tokens.name: heat-5
tokens.usage: Highest step of the sequential scale. Heat fills never carry text: the value goes in the tooltip or the inspector, so no text-on-heat pair exists.

tokens.name: syn-keyword
tokens.usage: Python keywords in the editor and code blocks (class, def, from, import, return).

tokens.name: syn-string
tokens.usage: String literals.

tokens.name: syn-number
tokens.usage: Number literals: kwarg values like 128 or 1e-4 are the numbers learners change most, so they get a clear hue.

tokens.name: syn-type
tokens.usage: Class names and block calls (Attention, RMSNorm, Decoder).

tokens.name: syn-comment
tokens.usage: Comments, in italic.

tokens.name: selection
tokens.usage: Text selection in the editor and in code blocks.

tokens.name: scrim
tokens.usage: Overlay behind a modal dialog.

families.sans: "IBM Plex Sans", "IBM Plex Sans Greek", system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
families.mono: "IBM Plex Mono", "IBM Plex Sans Greek", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

styles.name: title
styles.usage: Page title, once per page. The thing's own name, not a slogan.

styles.name: heading
styles.usage: Panel and section headings inside a page.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: The check compares your block with the reference on three random inputs.
styles.usage: Default interface text: forms, dialogs, descriptions.

styles.name: body-strong
styles.usage: Emphasis inside body text and button labels.

styles.name: small
styles.usage: Dense tables, run lists, compare rows, the queue.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Field labels and table headers. Sentence case; never uppercase, never letter-spaced.

styles.name: prose
styles.sample: Attention lets every token look back at the earlier ones and take a weighted average of what it finds.
styles.usage: Lesson text (lesson.md), at a measure of 68ch.

styles.name: prose-heading
styles.sample: Why divide by the square root of the head size

styles.name: readout
styles.usage: The one live number a page is about (current bpb on the run page). One or two per page at most.

styles.name: value
styles.usage: Every number, unit, shape, run ref, seed and hash in tables and text. Tabular figures.

styles.name: value-strong
styles.usage: A value that is the subject of its row (the delta in a compare row).

styles.name: code-small
styles.usage: Equivalent commands and inline kwargs on graph nodes.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Glyph to word inside a tag; label to field.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Between controls in a row; cell padding (horizontal) in dense tables.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Panel padding in dense panels; between fields in a form.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Panel padding; page side gutter on a phone.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Between panels; page side gutter on desktop.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Between page sections; above a page title.

tokens.name: space-7
tokens.usage: Around an empty state's block. Rarely anywhere else.

tokens.name: radius-0
tokens.usage: Tables, plot areas, the top bar, panels that touch an edge.

tokens.name: radius-1
tokens.usage: State tags, lock marks, inline code, drop slots.

tokens.name: radius-2
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs, panels, graph nodes, the level switch.

tokens.name: radius-3
tokens.usage: Popovers, menus and dialogs. The largest radius in the system; nothing is pill-shaped.

shadow.note: Elevation is for things that float over other content. Panels on the page use a line border and no shadow.

tokens.name: shadow-pop
tokens.usage: Popovers, menus, tooltips, dialogs.

tokens.name: shadow-drag
tokens.usage: The block being dragged from the palette. Nothing else.

size.note: Fixed sizes for controls and rows. Density is one scale (no compact/comfortable toggle).

tokens.name: control-sm
tokens.usage: Icon buttons in toolbars and table rows.

tokens.name: control
tokens.usage: Default height of buttons, inputs, selects and the level switch.

tokens.name: control-lg
tokens.usage: The one primary action of a lesson page (Start, Train, Check).

tokens.name: row
tokens.usage: Dense table row height (runs, compare, queue, components).

tokens.name: topbar
tokens.usage: Height of the shell's top bar.

tokens.name: measure
tokens.usage: Maximum width of lesson prose.

tokens.name: sidebar
tokens.usage: Width of the block palette and the lesson outline.

tokens.name: inspector
tokens.usage: Width of the graph inspector and the run page's side column.

breakpoint.note: Desktop-first. Designed at wide, usable at narrow; below narrow only the watch screens (run, runs, queue, lesson reading) adapt.

tokens.name: bp-phone
tokens.usage: Below this, the shell collapses to a menu and watch screens stack to one column.

tokens.name: bp-narrow
tokens.usage: The smallest width the editor, graph and study builder support; below it they show 'Open on a larger screen'.

tokens.name: bp-wide
tokens.usage: The width every screen is designed at first.
